title: Functions over arrays
instructions:
## Pass the array, loop with an index

Write three functions that work on an array of numbers the way C++ functions work on a `double[]` with a length.

1. `mean(values)`: the arithmetic mean; `0` for an empty array.
2. `maxIndex(values)`: the index of the largest value (the first one if there is a tie); `-1` for an empty array.
3. `reverseInPlace(values)`: reverse the array **in place** by swapping ends towards the middle, and return the same array.

Use a `for` loop with an index; do not use `reverse()`, `Math.max` or `reduce`. This course uses C++; the browser cannot compile C, so the logic is practised here in JavaScript, which has the same loops, arrays and functions. Translate it to C afterwards.
hints: Sum with a loop, then divide by values.length; check for length 0 first.
Keep the best index so far; replace it only when values[i] > values[best].
for (let i = 0; i < Math.floor(n / 2); i++) swap values[i] with values[n - 1 - i].

checks.label: No reverse(), Math.max or reduce
checks.message: Write the loops yourself; that is the point of the exercise.

realityNote: In C++ the array does not know its own length, so the function takes `double values[], int n`, and reversing in place is the same two-index swap. std::reverse and std::max_element exist, but you are expected to know what they do inside.
